# Memory and Latent World Models\chaptersubtitle{Dynamic Frame Trees, Persistence Beyond Occlusion, and JEPAs}

![**Systems Organ Focus:** Stage 3 (Temporal Memory & Latent World Models) across the Proposal–Permission Privilege Boundary. Physical AI systems maintain time-indexed $SE(3)$ coordinate frame trees, estimate latent state transitions via JEPAs and RSSMs, and propagate spatial uncertainty bounds across sensory occlusions.](figures/fig_pipeline_locator.svg){#fig-locator-ch06 width=100% fig-pos="H"}

*Why does an autonomous mobile manipulator drop a delicate glass object the moment an obstacle occludes the overhead camera?*

In digital simulation, the physical state of every entity is permanently accessible in global memory arrays. In the physical world, sensory contact is intermittent: objects pass behind occlusions, sensors suffer dropouts, and cameras are blinded by the robot's own moving linkages. Because observation is not state ($o_t \neq x_t$), an embodied agent cannot rely solely on instantaneous sensory snapshots. Nor can it afford the computational cost of generating raw video pixels in real time. Instead, it must maintain a structured, latent representation of physical reality, anchored by time-indexed coordinate frame trees in $SE(3)$, forward predictive dynamics in compact latent space, and expanding spatial uncertainty envelopes that mathematically enforce when memory expires.

{{< pagebreak >}}

After studying this chapter, you will be able to:

1. Formulate the physical POMDP gap to explain why raw observations are incomplete ($o_t \neq x_t$) due to occlusions, transduction noise, and transport delays.
2. Construct dynamic $SE(3)$ coordinate trees and execute singularity-free continuous integration in Lie algebra tangent space $\mathfrak{se}(3)$ via matrix exponentials.
3. Deploy continuous-discrete Extended Kalman Filters using the Joseph-form covariance stability contract and Mahalanobis outlier gating in static SRAM (`malloc = 0`).
4. Implement Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) and Recurrent State-Space Models (RSSMs) to forecast multi-step physical transitions without generating video pixels.
5. Quantify epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty using deep ensembles and latent variance heads to trigger safe operational fallbacks.
6. Calculate the Maximum Occlusion Horizon ($t_{\text{max}}$) from spatial clearance margins and target drift velocity to enforce hard Time-To-Live (TTL) state leases.
7. Dissect coordinate synchronization failures where uncompensated transform latency skews spatial targets and damages physical tooling.
8. Author the formal state-and-timing interface specification (**STATE-01**) establishing coordinate hierarchies, TTL validity leases, and zero-allocation ring buffers.

**Core Chapter Takeaway:** Observation is never true physical state ($o_t \neq x_t$). Robust physical agency requires maintaining explicit spatiotemporal coordinate transforms alongside latent world models that predict multi-step physical transitions while bounding uncertainty under partial observability.
:::


## The Fundamental Gap: Why Observation Is Not State Under Partial Observability

In classical digital computing, information stored in memory remains static, exact, and permanently accessible until explicitly overwritten. In reinforcement learning theory and cloud-hosted foundation models, software agents routinely operate under the idealized assumption of a fully observable Markov Decision Process (MDP), wherein the observation received by the agent is mathematically identical to the true environmental state ($o_t \equiv x_t$).

In Physical AI, this assumption is completely invalid. The physical universe operates as a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP), formally defined by the tuple $\mathcal{M} = \langle \mathcal{S}, \mathcal{A}, \mathcal{T}, \mathcal{R}, \Omega, \mathcal{O}, \gamma \rangle$, where $\mathcal{S}$ represents the continuous, unobserved physical world state ($W_t \in \mathcal{S}$), $\mathcal{A}$ is the action space of commanded actuator forces, $\mathcal{T}(s' \mid s, a)$ is the true environmental transition probability governed by Newtonian mechanics and thermodynamics, $\Omega$ is the observation space of digitized sensor bytes, and $\mathcal{O}(o \mid s')$ is the observation emission probability.

The physical observation $o_t \in \Omega$ captured by onboard sensors is fundamentally distinct from the true physical state $x_t \in \mathcal{S}$. When a 6-DoF robotic arm reaches toward a component on an assembly workbench, the manipulator's own mechanical forearm inevitably passes between the camera and the workpiece. For hundreds of milliseconds, zero optical photons reach the sensor ($o_t = \emptyset$). The physical object does not dissolve; it continues to occupy space, possess mass, and present a rigid collision boundary. A purely reactive policy that maps $o_t \to a_t$ collapses instantaneously, losing spatial tracking and commanding erratic motions.

Furthermore, physical sensors capture corrupted, low-dimensional projections of continuous physical fields. A single 2D camera frame captures projected luminance but lacks direct metric depth, object velocities, contact friction coefficients, and internal motor winding temperatures. Compounding this incompleteness, sensor exposure times, serialization buses, and memory contention introduce transport latencies ($\Delta t_{\text{transport}}$), meaning an observation arriving in digital memory at time $t$ reflects the physical world as it existed in the past.

To maintain metric consistency across these physical constraints, an embodied agent requires a structured geometric backbone. It builds time-indexed kinematic coordinate trees in $SE(3)$ that map transformations between sensor frames and physical linkages without rotational singularities (Section 6.2). 

To track dynamic states across high-rate proprioceptive streams and asynchronous exteroceptive updates, the agent relies on continuous-discrete estimators executing on embedded silicon (Section 6.3). These estimators apply numerical stability contracts and outlier rejection gates within fixed SRAM allocations to prevent memory fragmentation.

In unconstrained environments where rigid geometric models fail, the system transitions to compact latent world models (Section 6.4). By predicting dynamics within abstract embedding spaces rather than rendering pixel bitmaps, the agent forecasts transitions efficiently, neutralizes deliberation latency, and bounds spatial uncertainty growth over time.

When coordinate synchronization or uncertainty bounds fail, temporal skew directly produces physical collisions (Section 6.5). Preventing these failures requires rigorous state-and-timing interface contracts that govern coordinate hierarchies and revoke stale proposals.

| Canonical Archetype | State Persistence Focus | Dominant Uncertainty Factor | Frame Tree Root |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Mobility** | Ego-localization and dynamic obstacle tracking | Global position drift and wheel slip over wide terrain | `map` (Earth-fixed) |
| **Contact Manipulation** | Tool-tip tracking and workpiece coordinate geometry | Sub-millimeter mechanical backlash and transport latency skew | `robot_base` (Static mount) |
| **Cybernetic Process** | Actuator thermal capacitance and chemical states | Unobserved internal energy buildup and ambient heat dissipation | `thermal_mass` (Internal) |

: The State Persistence Matrix across Physical AI Archetypes. Diverse physical systems anchor coordinate hierarchies differently, yet all experience temporal uncertainty expansion when direct observation is lost. {#tbl-state-persistence-archetypes}

To act competently under partial observability, an embodied agent cannot rely on instantaneous sensor snapshots alone (@tbl-state-persistence-archetypes). It must maintain a persistent, internal state belief distribution $b_t(s) = p(s_t \mid o_{1:t}, a_{1:t-1})$. This belief distribution bridges sensory dropouts, fuses asynchronous measurements into a unified coordinate frame, and continuously bounds the expansion of spatial uncertainty over time.


## Coordinate Metrology: Dynamic Frame Trees, Kinematic Chains, and Lie Algebra Tangent Spaces

To maintain a geometrically consistent model of the physical environment, an embodied agent must track the continuous spatial relationships between its base chassis, articulated linkages, mounted sensors, and external workspace objects. This geometric metrology is formalized through Dynamic Kinematic Coordinate Frame Trees ($\mathcal{T}_{\text{frames}}$), where nodes represent spatial coordinate systems and directed edges represent rigid geometric transformations (@fig-se3-frame-tree).

![**Dynamic $SE(3)$ Kinematic Frame Tree.** Coordinate frame hierarchies spanning the static world frame, robot base, articulated joint links, camera optical sensors, and target object grasp frames. Transforming coordinates across the tree requires composing homogeneous transformation matrices $\mathbf{T} \in SE(3)$ and integrating continuous velocity twists in Lie algebra tangent space $\mathfrak{se}(3)$ without gimbal lock singularities.](figures/fig05_se3_frame_tree.svg){#fig-se3-frame-tree width=100%}

The spatial relationship between any parent frame $A$ and child frame $B$ is a member of the Special Euclidean Group $SE(3)$, represented as a $4 \times 4$ homogeneous transformation matrix comprising an orthonormal rotation matrix $\mathbf{R}_B^A \in SO(3)$ and a translational position vector $\mathbf{p}_B^A \in \mathbb{R}^3$:

$$\mathbf{T}_B^A = \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{R}_B^A & \mathbf{p}_B^A \\ \mathbf{0}^T & 1 \end{bmatrix} \in SE(3), \qquad \mathbf{R}_B^A \in SO(3) \implies (\mathbf{R}_B^A)^T \mathbf{R}_B^A = \mathbf{I}, \quad \det(\mathbf{R}_B^A) = +1$$

In classical software systems, engineers frequently represent 3D orientations using Euler angles (roll, pitch, yaw) or unit quaternions. However, Euler angles suffer from mathematical singularities known as gimbal lock, wherein the loss of one rotational degree of freedom paralyzes numerical trajectory optimization. Quaternions avoid gimbal lock but require continuous normalization ($\|\mathbf{q}\| = 1$), which discrete numerical integration algorithms distort over extended operating horizons.

### Matrix Exponential Integration in Lie Algebra Tangent Space

Physical AI architectures resolve rotational singularities by executing continuous temporal integration directly in the Lie Algebra Tangent Space $\mathfrak{se}(3)$ [@murray2017mathematical; @barfoot2017state]. A tangent-space velocity twist vector $\boldsymbol{\xi} \in \mathbb{R}^6$ packages both translational velocity $\mathbf{v} \in \mathbb{R}^3$ and angular velocity $\boldsymbol{\omega} \in \mathbb{R}^3$:

$$\boldsymbol{\xi} = \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{v} \\ \boldsymbol{\omega} \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^6, \qquad \boldsymbol{\xi}^\wedge = \begin{bmatrix} \boldsymbol{\omega}^\wedge & \mathbf{v} \\ \mathbf{0}^T & 0 \end{bmatrix} \in \mathfrak{se}(3)$$

The skew-symmetric matrix $\boldsymbol{\omega}^\wedge \in \mathfrak{so}(3)$ represents the cross-product operator for angular velocity:

$$\boldsymbol{\omega}^\wedge = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & -\omega_z & \omega_y \\ \omega_z & 0 & -\omega_x \\ -\omega_y & \omega_x & 0 \end{bmatrix} \in \mathfrak{so}(3)$$

The matrix exponential $\exp(\boldsymbol{\xi}^\wedge \Delta t): \mathfrak{se}(3) \to SE(3)$ maps continuous velocity twists onto smooth, singularity-free rigid-body transformations:

$$\mathbf{T}(t + \Delta t) = \mathbf{T}(t) \cdot \exp\left( \boldsymbol{\xi}^\wedge \Delta t \right)$$

Evaluating the matrix exponential in closed form yields:

$$\exp\left( \boldsymbol{\xi}^\wedge \Delta t \right) = \begin{bmatrix} \exp(\boldsymbol{\omega}^\wedge \Delta t) & \mathbf{V}\mathbf{v}\Delta t \\ \mathbf{0}^T & 1 \end{bmatrix}$$

where the left-Jacobian matrix $\mathbf{V}$ and rotation matrix $\exp(\boldsymbol{\omega}^\wedge \Delta t)$ are computed via Rodrigues formula with $\theta = \|\boldsymbol{\omega}\|\Delta t$:

$$\exp(\boldsymbol{\omega}^\wedge \Delta t) = \mathbf{I} + \frac{\sin\theta}{\theta}\boldsymbol{\omega}^\wedge + \frac{1 - \cos\theta}{\theta^2}(\boldsymbol{\omega}^\wedge)^2$$

$$\mathbf{V} = \mathbf{I} + \frac{1 - \cos\theta}{\theta^2}\boldsymbol{\omega}^\wedge + \frac{\theta - \sin\theta}{\theta^3}(\boldsymbol{\omega}^\wedge)^2$$

### Kinematic Serial Chains and Metric Grounding

Along an articulated kinematic serial chain with $N$ actuated joints, forward kinematics evaluates the end-effector tool pose $\mathbf{T}_{\text{tool}}^{\text{world}}$ by composing individual link transformations parameterized by measured joint angles $\mathbf{q} = [q_1, q_2, \dots, q_N]^T$:

$$\mathbf{T}_{\text{tool}}^{\text{world}}(\mathbf{q}) = \mathbf{T}_{\text{base}}^{\text{world}} \cdot \mathbf{T}_1^{\text{base}}(q_1) \cdot \mathbf{T}_2^1(q_2) \cdots \mathbf{T}_N^{N-1}(q_N) \cdot \mathbf{T}_{\text{tool}}^N$$

This dynamic frame tree serves as the foundational metric backbone for all spatial reasoning. When a high-level vision model detects an object affordance in camera optical coordinates ($\mathbf{P}_C$), the kinematic state engine resolves the target in the robot base frame ($\mathbf{P}_B$) by traversing the active transform tree:

$$\begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{P}_B \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} = \mathbf{T}_{\text{mount}}^B \cdot \mathbf{T}_{\text{camera}}^{\text{mount}} \cdot \begin{bmatrix} \mathbf{P}_C \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$

If any transformation along this kinematic chain is queried using an asynchronous or out-of-date timestamp without spatial covariance tracking, the resulting coordinate multiplication injects spatial skew that drives downstream end-effectors into physical obstacles.


## Classical State Estimation: The Extended Kalman Filter and Real-Time Silicon Execution

Embodied systems constantly manage a temporal mismatch between sensory channels. Proprioceptive joint encoders and IMU gyroscopes stream at $1000\text{ Hz}$ with sub-millisecond latencies, whereas exteroceptive cameras and depth sensors deliver frames at $30\text{ Hz}$ with $30\text{--}60\text{ ms}$ of transport and processing delay. During the $33.3\text{ ms}$ blind window between camera frames, a manipulator moving at $1.0\text{ m/s}$ travels $33.3\text{ mm}$, a displacement large enough to crush tooling or miss a grasping target.

To maintain a continuous state belief at $1000\text{ Hz}$, Physical AI systems employ continuous-discrete Extended Kalman Filters (EKF) [@kalman1960new; @thrun2005probabilistic]. The filter propagates high-rate state estimates forward between measurement arrivals and incorporates delayed, asynchronous exteroceptive observations whenever they become available.

### Continuous-Discrete Formulation and Propagation Dynamics

The system state vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ evolves according to non-linear physical dynamics driven by control input $\mathbf{u}(t)$ and continuous process noise $\mathbf{w}(t) \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{Q}(t))$:

$$\dot{\mathbf{x}}(t) = f(\mathbf{x}(t), \mathbf{u}(t)) + \mathbf{w}(t)$$

Between discrete measurement arrivals, the continuous state estimate $\hat{\mathbf{x}}$ and error covariance matrix $\mathbf{P} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ propagate forward in time:

$$\dot{\hat{\mathbf{x}}}(t) = f(\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t), \mathbf{u}(t)), \qquad \dot{\mathbf{P}}(t) = \mathbf{F}(t)\mathbf{P}(t) + \mathbf{P}(t)\mathbf{F}(t)^T + \mathbf{Q}(t)$$

where $\mathbf{F}(t) = \left. \frac{\partial f}{\partial \mathbf{x}} \right|_{\hat{\mathbf{x}}(t), \mathbf{u}(t)}$ is the continuous-time state transition Jacobian. Full derivations of the error dynamics and continuous Riccati differential equations are provided in Appendix C.2.

When a discrete sensory observation $\mathbf{z}_k \in \mathbb{R}^m$ arrives at time $t_k$ with measurement noise $\mathbf{v}_k \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{R}_k)$, the estimator computes the measurement innovation $\mathbf{y}_k$ and innovation covariance $\mathbf{S}_k$:

$$\mathbf{y}_k = \mathbf{z}_k - h(\hat{\mathbf{x}}_k^-), \qquad \mathbf{S}_k = \mathbf{H}_k \mathbf{P}_k^- \mathbf{H}_k^T + \mathbf{R}_k$$

where $\mathbf{H}_k = \left. \frac{\partial h}{\partial \mathbf{x}} \right|_{\hat{\mathbf{x}}_k^-}$ is the measurement Jacobian. The optimal Kalman gain $\mathbf{K}_k$ balances model confidence against sensor precision:

$$\mathbf{K}_k = \mathbf{P}_k^- \mathbf{H}_k^T \mathbf{S}_k^{-1}$$

$$\hat{\mathbf{x}}_k^+ = \hat{\mathbf{x}}_k^- + \mathbf{K}_k \mathbf{y}_k$$

### The Joseph-Form Stability Contract on Embedded Silicon

In textbook derivations, the a posteriori covariance update is written as $\mathbf{P}_k^+ = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{K}_k \mathbf{H}_k)\mathbf{P}_k^-$. While algebraically compact, this standard form is numerically unstable on resource-constrained embedded microcontrollers utilizing 32-bit floating-point (FP32) arithmetic. Subtracting large positive matrices under FP32 truncation causes $\mathbf{P}_k^+$ to lose symmetry ($\mathbf{P} \neq \mathbf{P}^T$) and positive definiteness ($\exists \mathbf{v}: \mathbf{v}^T \mathbf{P} \mathbf{v} < 0$). Once positive definiteness is lost, the filter treats variances as negative quantities, causing the gain calculation to diverge and commanding unbounded control signals.

To prevent numerical divergence on embedded targets, Physical AI runtimes mandate the Joseph-form covariance update:

$$\mathbf{P}_k^+ = (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{K}_k \mathbf{H}_k)\mathbf{P}_k^- (\mathbf{I} - \mathbf{K}_k \mathbf{H}_k)^T + \mathbf{K}_k \mathbf{R}_k \mathbf{K}_k^T$$

The Joseph formulation is structurally guaranteed to remain symmetric and positive semi-definite for any gain matrix $\mathbf{K}_k$, because both additive terms are symmetric quadratic forms ($\mathbf{A} \mathbf{P} \mathbf{A}^T$ and $\mathbf{B} \mathbf{R} \mathbf{B}^T$). 

To reject corrupted sensory outliers, such as optical reflections, dynamic dust, or multi-path LiDAR reflections, the filter evaluates the squared Mahalanobis distance of the innovation before applying the state update:

$$d_M^2 = \mathbf{y}_k^T \mathbf{S}_k^{-1} \mathbf{y}_k \le \chi_{m, 1-\alpha}^2$$

If $d_M^2$ exceeds the chi-squared threshold for $m$ degrees of freedom at significance level $\alpha$ (typically $\chi_{3, 0.99}^2 = 11.34$), the measurement is gated and discarded, preserving the integrity of the state belief.

### Static SRAM Ring Buffers and Microsecond Timestamp Propagation

Embedded state estimation must execute deterministically without dynamic memory allocation (`malloc = 0`). On an ARM Cortex-M7 or RISC-V microcontroller operating at $480\text{ MHz}$, dynamic heap allocation introduces memory fragmentation, unpredictable garbage collection pauses, and non-deterministic execution times that violate hard real-time deadlines.

For a 12-state kinematic filter ($\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^{12}$ representing 3D position, orientation angles, linear velocities, and angular rates), the state vector occupies $48\text{ Bytes}$ and the covariance matrix $\mathbf{P} \in \mathbb{R}^{12 \times 12}$ occupies $576\text{ Bytes}$ in FP32 format. The complete estimator state footprint is under $2\text{ KB}$ of static SRAM, fitting entirely within the processor's tightly coupled data memory (DTCM).

State histories are maintained in fixed-size circular ring buffers indexed by 64-bit IEEE 1588 Precision Time Protocol (PTP) hardware timestamps. When an asynchronous camera observation with capture timestamp $t_{\text{capture}} = t_{\text{now}} - 45\text{ ms}$ arrives, the estimator rewinds its state history in the ring buffer, applies the measurement update at the exact historical epoch, and re-propagates forward to $t_{\text{now}}$ using stored proprioceptive inputs. This deterministic update completes within a worst-case execution time ($\text{WCET}$) of less than $150\ \mu\text{s}$, guaranteeing sub-millisecond control loop determinism at $1000\text{ Hz}$.


## Latent World Models and Uncertainty Propagation: JEPAs, RSSMs, and Horizon Degradation

While classical Kalman filters excel at tracking parameterized rigid-body kinematics, they cannot scale to open-world physical scenes containing deformable fabrics, splashing fluids, granular media, or unstructured clutter. An embodied agent needs a world model capable of predicting how complex environments evolve under candidate action sequences.

In recent literature, generative video models have been proposed to forecast futures by synthesizing uncompressed RGB pixels frame by frame. On an embodied physical platform, autoregressive pixel generation is an inefficient architectural choice (@fig-world-model-paradigms):

1. **Computational Arithmetic Overhead:** Generating $1080\text{p}$ video at 30 FPS requires greater than $10^{13}\text{ FLOPs/s}$, saturating dynamic RAM buses and inducing thermal throttling on mobile compute platforms.
2. **Visual Hallucinations:** Pixel decoders frequently synthesize plausible textures while hallucinating nonexistent free space or erasing thin, rigid obstacles. Commanding high-energy actuators based on hallucinated geometry leads directly to structural collisions.
3. **Irrelevant Entropy Consumption:** A pixel-level generative model expends capacity predicting high-frequency visual noise, such as swaying grass, water ripples, or shadow movement, which carries zero functional relevance for physical manipulation.

![**Latent World Model Paradigms in Physical AI.** (Top) Generative video world models waste immense compute generating uncompressed pixels prone to visual hallucinations. (Bottom) Non-generative Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) and Recurrent State-Space Models (RSSMs) predict state transitions strictly within compact, metric latent embedding spaces ($\mathbf{z} \in \mathbb{R}^d$), achieving microsecond execution speeds with zero pixel overhead.](figures/fig05_world_model_paradigms.svg){#fig-world-model-paradigms width=100%}

### Non-Generative World Modeling via Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures

Physical AI avoids pixel rendering by utilizing Latent World Models. These architectures predict environmental dynamics entirely within compact, information-dense latent representation spaces $\mathbf{z} \in \mathcal{Z} \subset \mathbb{R}^d$, discarding task-irrelevant visual entropy while preserving the underlying physical invariants.

Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) provide a non-generative framework for self-supervised physical world modeling [@assran2023self; @lecun2022path]. A JEPA maps an observation $o_t$ into a compact latent vector $\mathbf{z}_t = E_\theta(o_t) \in \mathbb{R}^d$. Given candidate physical actions $\mathbf{a}_{t:t+H}$, a latent transition predictor $P_\phi$ forecasts future representations:

$$\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1} = P_\phi(\mathbf{z}_t, \mathbf{a}_t)$$

To train the predictive network without contrastive negative samples or pixel decoders, JEPAs deploy an asymmetric student-teacher architecture. The context encoder $E_\theta$ processes visible observations, while the target encoder $E_\psi$ produces stable target representations for future states. To prevent representational collapse (where the encoder maps all inputs to a trivial constant vector), the target encoder parameters $\psi$ are not updated via gradients; instead, they track the context encoder via an Exponential Moving Average (EMA):

$$\psi \leftarrow \tau \psi + (1 - \tau) \theta, \qquad \tau \in [0.99, 0.999]$$

Trained under an $L_2$ representation loss $L_{\text{JEPA}} = \|\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1} - E_\psi(o_{t+1})\|_2^2$, the model learns to discard unpredictable visual background patterns and encode only the causal physical dynamics governing the scene.

### Forward State Projection to Neutralize Deliberation Latency

A major systems bottleneck in physical control is deliberation latency. High-capacity reasoners and trajectory optimizers require $100\text{--}500\text{ ms}$ of compute time ($t_{\text{deliberate}}$) to synthesize action proposals. If an optimizer computes a trajectory starting from the current observed state $x_t$, the resulting action plan is already obsolete by the time it reaches the motor drivers at $t + t_{\text{deliberate}}$.

Latent world models neutralize deliberation latency through forward state projection. Prior to initiating trajectory optimization, the latent predictor rolls the state belief forward across the expected computation and transport delay:

$$\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t + t_{\text{deliberate}}} = P_\phi^{(k)}(\mathbf{z}_t, \mathbf{a}_{t:t + t_{\text{deliberate}}})$$

Conditioned on this projected future state, the planner optimizes actions $\mathbf{a}_{t + t_{\text{deliberate}} : t + t_{\text{deliberate}} + H}$, ensuring that the planned trajectory matches the physical configuration of the robot at the exact moment execution begins.

To maintain temporal persistence across extended multi-step occlusions, Recurrent State-Space Models (RSSMs) maintain a dual latent state [@ha2018worldmodels; @hafner2023mastering]:

$$\text{Deterministic Recurrent State:} \quad h_t = f_\phi(h_{t-1}, s_{t-1}, a_{t-1})$$

$$\text{Stochastic Latent Belief:} \quad s_t \sim q_\psi(s_t \mid h_t, o_t) \quad (\text{Posterior}), \qquad \hat{s}_t \sim p_\theta(\hat{s}_t \mid h_t) \quad (\text{Prior})$$

During sensory dropouts ($o_t = \emptyset$), the RSSM transitions from filtering to open-loop imagination by updating its state using the prior distribution $p_\theta(\hat{s}_t \mid h_t)$, enabling the robot to track physical interactions through occlusions.

### Quantifying Epistemic Disagreement with Deep Ensembles

Before commanding high-power actuators, an embodied agent must evaluate its own prediction uncertainty. Physical prediction entails two distinct forms of uncertainty:

1. **Aleatoric Uncertainty (Physical Stochasticity):** Inherent physical randomness in the environment, such as ground friction variations on loose gravel or analog sensor noise. Aleatoric uncertainty cannot be eliminated through additional training data; it is parameterized directly via Gaussian variance heads $\sigma_{\text{aleatoric}}^2$.
2. **Epistemic Uncertainty (Model Ignorance):** Lack of model knowledge regarding unfamiliar dynamics, unmodeled payload shifts, or out-of-distribution physical geometries.

To quantify epistemic uncertainty on embedded hardware, architectures deploy Deep Ensemble Latent World Models. An ensemble of $M$ transition heads $\{P_{\phi_m}\}_{m=1}^M$ is trained with distinct weight initializations. Given latent state $\mathbf{z}_t$ and action $\mathbf{a}_t$, each head outputs an independent forecast $\hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1}^{(m)}$.

The ensemble mean represents the expected physical transition:

$$\bar{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1} = \frac{1}{M} \sum_{m=1}^M \hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1}^{(m)}$$

The epistemic uncertainty corresponds to the empirical variance across ensemble forecasts:

$$\sigma_{\text{epistemic}}^2(t+1) = \frac{1}{M-1} \sum_{m=1}^M \left\| \hat{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1}^{(m)} - \bar{\mathbf{z}}_{t+1} \right\|_2^2$$

When the robot operates in familiar regimes, ensemble predictions align closely ($\sigma_{\text{epistemic}} \to 0$). When encountering an unfamiliar physical regime (such as unexpected tool slippage or extreme mechanical compliance), ensemble predictions diverge. If $\sigma_{\text{epistemic}}$ exceeds a calibrated threshold $\sigma_{\text{safe\_ceiling}}$, the supervisor revokes active intent proposals and commands a safe operational hold.

### The Information Decay Principle and the Maximum Occlusion Horizon

A fundamental law of physical systems is that open-loop forward predictions degrade over time. In non-linear dynamical systems, two trajectories originating from nearby states diverge exponentially at a rate governed by the system's maximal Lyapunov exponent $\lambda_{\text{max}}$:

$$\|\delta \mathbf{x}(t)\| \approx \|\delta \mathbf{x}_0\| e^{\lambda_{\text{max}} t}$$

In robotics, this divergence manifests as rapid spatial uncertainty growth when sensory feedback is interrupted (@fig-uncertainty-expansion).

![**Spatial Uncertainty Covariance Expansion Under Occlusion.** The physical spatial confidence ellipse expands monotonically over time when direct optical observation is lost ($\sigma_{\text{pos}}(t) = \sigma_0 + v_{\text{target}} \cdot \Delta t$). When the uncertainty boundary breaches available clearance ($d_{\text{clearance}} - d_{\text{margin}}$), the active State TTL Lease irrevocably expires, triggering a deterministic Category 2 safe hold.](figures/fig05_uncertainty_expansion.svg){#fig-uncertainty-expansion width=100%}

When a moving target passes behind an obstruction ($o_t = \emptyset$), the object does not vanish. Its true position drifts within an expanding uncertainty envelope. Assuming a maximum target velocity $v_{\text{target\_max}}$, the position uncertainty standard deviation expands linearly over time:

$$\sigma_{\text{pos}}(\Delta t) = \sigma_0 + v_{\text{target\_max}} \cdot \Delta t$$

Given an available spatial clearance $d_{\text{clearance}}$ to surrounding obstacles and a required safety margin $d_{\text{margin}}$, setting the upper bound of the spatial confidence envelope equal to the allowable clearance defines the **Maximum Occlusion Horizon ($t_{\text{max}}$)**:

$$\sigma_{\text{pos}}(t_{\text{max}}) \le d_{\text{clearance}} - d_{\text{margin}} \implies t_{\text{max}} = \frac{d_{\text{clearance}} - d_{\text{margin}} - \sigma_0}{v_{\text{target\_max}}}$$

If a sensory occlusion lasts longer than $t_{\text{max}}$, the spatial uncertainty envelope breaches safe physical limits. At this exact threshold, the state estimate's Time-To-Live (TTL) lease expires, forcing the system to halt motion before a collision can occur.


## Systems Failure Anatomy and the State-and-Timing Interface

The consequences of uncompensated coordinate transform latency are illustrated by an industrial incident involving a high-speed precision manipulator.

::: {.callout-autopsy title="The Stale Frame Tree Collision"}
* **System:** 6-DoF Precision Articulated Manipulator operating at $v = 0.9\text{ m/s}$ in an industrial surface-mount assembly cell.
* **Incident:** Vacuum gripper collided with an aluminum assembly fixture at $0.9\text{ m/s}$, delivering an impact force of $1.8\text{ kN}$ that shattered ceramic vacuum tooling and damaged internal load cells ($3,200\text{ USD}$ repair cost).
* **Telemetry Snapshot:** Forearm link occluded wrist camera for $180\text{ ms}$; transform lookup returned cached coordinates aged $65\text{ ms}$; vertical coordinate error reached $5.85\text{ cm}$; impact occurred at $T + 0.000\text{ s}$.
* **Root Cause:** The kinematic state engine evaluated target coordinates by multiplying real-time joint positions ($t_{\text{now}}$) by a stale camera transform ($t_{\text{now}} - 65\text{ ms}$) without time-matching interpolation or covariance expansion.
* **Architectural Flaw:** Absence of time-indexed transform interpolation in Lie algebra tangent space and lack of hard Time-To-Live (TTL) state validity leases.
* **Provenance:** Engineered composite drawn from documented industrial manipulator incidents; telemetry constructed for teaching.
:::

![The 6-DoF Precision Articulated Manipulator Platform. Deployed in high-density surface-mount electronics assembly with wrist-mounted depth cameras and vacuum tooling. Fusing stale transform coordinates ($65\text{ ms}$ old) with real-time joint encoders without expanding spatial covariance caused a destructive collision with an aluminum fixture block.](figures/fig05_manipulator_arm_cropped.jpg){#fig-manipulator-arm width=100%}

### Forensic Breakdown of the Stale Transform Skew

In this incident, the 6-DoF articulated manipulator was descending toward a printed circuit board (PCB) fixture at $v = 0.9\text{ m/s}$ (@fig-manipulator-arm). During the descent, the robot's third linkage rotated across the field of view of the wrist camera, occluding the PCB alignment fiducials for $180\text{ ms}$.

The software flaw resided in the coordinate transform lookup buffer. The state engine was configured to query the camera-to-target transform $\mathbf{T}_{\text{target}}^{\text{cam}}$ without enforcing strict timestamp matching. Because the vision pipeline stalled during the occlusion, the transform lookup returned the last cached transform from $65\text{ ms}$ prior, while joint angle encoders were sampled synchronously at $t_{\text{now}}$.

The kinematic engine calculated target position in base coordinates by multiplying non-isochronous transforms:

$$\mathbf{T}_{\text{target}}^{\text{base}}(t_{\text{now}}) = \mathbf{T}_{\text{cam}}^{\text{base}}(t_{\text{now}}) \cdot \mathbf{T}_{\text{target}}^{\text{cam}}(t_{\text{now}} - 65\text{ ms})$$

This temporal mismatch injected an uncompensated spatial skew along the vertical descent axis:

$$\Delta z_{\text{skew}} = v_{\text{descent}} \cdot \Delta t_{\text{stale}} = 0.9\text{ m/s} \times 0.065\text{ s} = 0.0585\text{ m} = 5.85\text{ cm}$$

Assuming the workpiece lay $5.85\text{ cm}$ below its true position, the trajectory planner commanded the manipulator to continue descending at high speed. The vacuum gripper struck the solid aluminum fixture at $0.9\text{ m/s}$, generating an instantaneous impact force of $1.8\text{ kN}$ that fractured the ceramic tip and sheared mounting pins (@tbl-telemetry-ch06).

| Timestamp | Subsystem & Substrate | Recorded State / Telemetry Event | Physical Implication |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **$T - 0.245\text{ s}$** | Wrist RGB-D Camera | Valid detection of PCB fiducials captured ($t_{\text{exp}} = 10\text{ ms}$). | Target coordinates valid in camera frame. |
| **$T - 0.180\text{ s}$** | Manipulator Forearm | Forearm linkage rotates into optical path, occluding camera for $180\text{ ms}$. | Zero optical photons reach sensor die. |
| **$T - 0.065\text{ s}$** | Kinematic State Engine | Stale transform $\mathbf{T}_{\text{target}}^{\text{cam}}$ ($65\text{ ms}$ old) multiplied with $t_{\text{now}}$ joint encoders. | Frame tree multiplication injects $5.85\text{ cm}$ spatial skew. |
| **$T - 0.010\text{ s}$** | Trajectory Planner | Planner interpolates descent targeting corrupted base coordinates. | Gripper descends at $0.9\text{ m/s}$ toward solid metal fixture. |
| **$T + 0.000\text{ s}$** | Vacuum Gripper Tooling | Tooling strikes aluminum fixture block ($1.8\text{ kN}$ dynamic impact). | Tooling shatters; vacuum seals destroyed ($3,200\text{ USD}$ overhaul). |

: Flight-Recorder Telemetry Ledger: The Stale Frame Tree Collision Incident. Tracing uncompensated coordinate latency to mechanical tooling destruction. {#tbl-telemetry-ch06}

To eliminate stale-transform collisions, Physical AI architectures enforce bounded SRAM ring buffers indexed by 64-bit PTP hardware timestamps. When querying a transform at time $t_{\text{query}}$, the state engine performs exact geodesic interpolation in Lie algebra space $\mathfrak{se}(3)$ between the bounding historical frames ($t_1 \le t_{\text{query}} \le t_2$). If the query timestamp exceeds the freshest recorded frame by more than the configured TTL lease ($\Delta t > \tau_{\text{ttl}}$), the lookup returns an explicit `TRANSFORM_EXPIRED` fault, forcing downstream planning to halt.

### Silent Failure Modes and Online Innovation Gating

State estimation subsystems frequently fail silently. Unlike software crashes that raise exceptions, a state estimator continues computing outputs even when its internal belief has drifted far from physical reality. A camera lens partially obscured by oil mist continues delivering images, but feature match scores degrade; an optical encoder experiencing vibration misses pulses, accumulating unobserved angular drift.

To detect silent failures online, the state supervisor monitors two runtime health metrics:

1. **Normalized Innovation Squared (NIS):** The filter continuously tracks the running average of the Mahalanobis distance across a sliding window of $N_w$ updates ($\bar{d}_M^2 = \frac{1}{N_w} \sum_{i=1}^{N_w} \mathbf{y}_i^T \mathbf{S}_i^{-1} \mathbf{y}_i$). If $\bar{d}_M^2$ consistently exceeds the $95\%$ confidence bounds of the theoretical $\chi^2$ distribution, the filter flags an unmodeled systematic bias or sensor decalibration.
2. **Transform Freshness Watchdogs:** Every frame tree node maintains a hardware countdown timer reset upon receipt of valid sensor packets. If the timer expires, downstream nodes are marked untrusted, preventing stale spatial transforms from propagating through kinematic chains.

### Structural Absorption in Monolithic Sensorimotor Policies

In modern end-to-end learning literature, monolithic Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models attempt to map image pixels directly to motor actions without explicit intermediate state estimation. In such architectures, temporal memory is absorbed into internal recurrent hidden states or transformer attention context windows.

While end-to-end absorption simplifies the software pipeline, it obscures physical invariants. A monolithic neural policy cannot provide mathematical guarantees regarding positive definite covariances, coordinate frame consistency, or maximum occlusion horizons. If the attention mechanism attends to irrelevant background features during an occlusion, the policy commands unconstrained control actions without raising an error.

In robust Physical AI design, even when an end-to-end model generates proposed trajectories on the application processor (MPU), the deterministic microcontroller (MCU) maintains an independent, explicit kinematic state filter. The MCU validates proposed trajectories against physical barrier invariants and spatial clearance bounds before granting motor execution authority.

| Parameter Category | Specification Key | Engineering Target Value | Verification Boundary |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Root Coordinate Frame** | `frame_graph.root_frame` | `world` | Static Euclidean origin $[0, 0, 0]^T$ |
| **Kinematic Base Frame** | `frame_graph.base_frame` | `robot_base` | Rigid physical mounting base |
| **Transform Interpolation** | `transform_buffer.max_history_ms` | $500.0\text{ ms}$ | Continuous circular ring buffer in SRAM |
| **Visual State TTL Lease** | `state_ttl_leases.visual_tracking_ttl_ms` | $100.0\text{ ms}$ | Revokes MPU proposal authority if $\Delta t > 100\text{ ms}$ |
| **Proprioceptive TTL Lease** | `state_ttl_leases.proprioceptive_ttl_ms` | $5.0\text{ ms}$ | MCU trips Category 2 safe stop if encoders drop |
| **Max Spatial Uncertainty** | `uncertainty_bounds.sigma_pos_max_mm` | $15.0\text{ mm}$ | Hard spatial confidence ceiling |
| **Anomaly Innovation Gate** | `anomaly_detection.mahalanobis_gate` | $3.0\sigma$ ($d_M \le 3.0$) | Rejects corrupt sensory detections / collisions |
| **Thermal Warning Knee** | `thermal_limits.warning_temp_c` | $85.0^\circ\text{C}$ | Initiates linear torque derating |
| **Thermal Emergency Cutoff** | `thermal_limits.critical_cutoff_c` | $105.0^\circ\text{C}$ | Immediate inverter bridge shutdown ($0\text{ Nm}$) |

::: {.callout-warning title="LLM Context Windows Substitute for Physical World Models"}
* **The Fallacy:** The internal latent representation or attention context window of a Multi-Modal LLM serves directly as an embodied world model.
* **The Physical Reality:** LLM context windows store token sequences, not metric spatial coordinates ($SE(3)$), Lie algebra velocity twists ($\mathfrak{se}(3)$), or physical mass distributions [@murray2017mathematical]. Autoregressive token generation lacks geometric invariance, metric scale calibration, and physical boundary enforcement.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Depth Cameras Deliver Metric Ground Truth Without Kinematic Tracking"}
* **The Fallacy:** A high-resolution depth camera provides ground-truth 3D coordinates without continuous extrinsic kinematic tracking.
* **The Physical Reality:** Camera mounting brackets flex and vibrate under mechanical robot accelerations ($>2g$). Without continuous extrinsic calibration tracking ($\mathbf{T}_{\text{camera}}^{\text{base}}$) and timestamp synchronization, static camera assumptions introduce centimeter-level metric grasp errors [@tobin2017domain; @peng2018sim].
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Zero Process Noise Guarantees Kalman Filter Convergence"}
* **The Fallacy:** A Kalman filter will never diverge as long as process noise covariance $\mathbf{Q}$ is set to an arbitrarily small value.
* **The Physical Reality:** Setting process noise $\mathbf{Q}$ artificially small makes the estimator overconfident in its internal physical model. When real-world disturbances occur, an overconfident filter rejects valid sensory innovation updates, causing the filter to diverge completely from physical reality [@thrun2005probabilistic].
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="State Estimation Belongs Entirely in User-Space Software"}
* **The Fallacy:** State estimation can execute entirely in user-space Python on the Linux application processor.
* **The Physical Reality:** If Linux experiences a background page fault, memory compaction stall, or kernel panic, user-space Python state estimation freezes. The bare-metal microcontroller must maintain an independent proprioceptive state estimator ($1000\text{ Hz}$) to compute dynamic stopping envelopes and execute safe hardware stops during MPU stalls.
:::


## Chapter Summary and Forward Handoff

This chapter established how embodied physical agents maintain structured spatial belief and temporal continuity across inevitable sensory occlusions. Physical state is not a stateless text token sequence safely confined to a digital context window; it is a metric, dynamic coordinate tree mathematically integrated in Lie algebra tangent space and strictly bounded by constantly expanding uncertainty covariances. By pairing advanced latent world models on high-performance compute arrays with deterministic hardware ring buffers and real-time proprioceptive state estimators on edge microcontrollers, systems engineers ensure that transient sensory blackouts never result in open-loop physical destruction.

Having firmly anchored the agent's perception into a mathematically sound, temporally persistent world model, the architectural pipeline is now primed to generate purposeful action. In the following chapter, **Chapter 7 (Intent and Reasoners: System 2 Multimodal VLAs, Spatial Grounding, and Expiring Intent Leases)**, we will explore how physical agents reason about task goals over these state beliefs. We will examine how high-level semantic instructions are translated into bounded, physically verified kinematic proposals, and how the system rigorously enforces expiring intent leases before authorizing multi-joint motion in the real world.
